steps.what: Evaluate students' motor needs through appropriate observation, interaction and review of relevant evidence
Determine the need for adapted physical education services within the specialist's authority

tasks.design: Retain direct assessment and the specialist's service-needs recommendation. Existing evidence in {DOCS} supports the decision without converting observed performance into an automatic eligibility outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: A motor need is contextual and cannot be established from a record label alone.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest supplies no validated automatic motor-needs assessment applicable to this task.
tasks.still_hard: Participation, physical constraints and assessment conditions can change the interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the individual, adapt the assessment and recognize when another professional must contribute.
tasks.altitude: Assessment and recommendation retain their full human time.

reach.task: Discuss evidence of a student's support needs
reach.learn: How observations translate into an educational support recommendation

evidence.claim: The digest retains disability strategies and adapting instruction as human work; it does not establish automated motor assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is educational assessment and recommendation, excluding medical diagnosis, formal admissions or entitlement decisions and subsequent service delivery. Local service authority must be established.

Students and caregivers supply accounts during s1; prior assessors provide existing evidence before s1 and the school supplies criteria before s2. Observation, clarification and existing capture remain within retained time. No free standardized motor score, diagnosis or eligibility flag is assumed.
Use existing assessment methods and native record access first. No new model, delegated data capture or added maintenance is proposed.
unknowns: Applicable assessment methods and service-decision authority
research_questions: Which findings require additional clinical or educational expertise before a recommendation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Direct motor assessment and service-needs judgement retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Establish understandable behavior standards and demonstrate safe participation routines
Maintain orderly learning through observation, reminders and proportionate responses to changing behavior

tasks.design: Retain explanation, demonstration and live supervision. Existing school guidance in {DOCS} supports consistent practice without replacing the specialist's physical presence or judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety and behavior change during the activity rather than arriving as complete structured records.
tasks.enabler_now: No administrative baseline or safe automatic supervision substitute is established.
tasks.still_hard: A useful response depends on the student's understanding, support needs and immediate surroundings.
tasks.human_edge: Notice emerging difficulty and respond supportively before it escalates.
tasks.altitude: Protect direct supervision and clear communication time.

reach.learn: How to give consistent assistance without assuming understanding

evidence.claim: Maintaining a safe adapted activity involves live observation and interaction; no measured automation saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is establishing and maintaining activity behavior standards, excluding formal discipline decisions and separate incident reporting.

The school provides expectations before s1. The specialist identifies support needs during explanation and observes current behavior during s2; its time includes checking understanding. No free safe-to-participate, compliant-behavior or emotion flag is assumed.
Use existing guidance and accessible demonstration first. No camera classification, emotion inference, new system or additional upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Actual activity risks and support staffing
research_questions: Which participation rules require a different demonstration or communication method?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Clear instruction and live supervision remain necessary; no separate paperwork share is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collaborate with educational personnel to develop feasible inclusive activities for children with disabilities

tasks.design: Retain reciprocal planning with the educational team and existing activity information in {DOCS}. A generated activity description cannot establish whether staff, facilities and individual support will make participation feasible.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inclusive provision depends on shared expertise and practical constraints across staff.
tasks.enabler_now: The supplied planning tools do not demonstrate replacement of that collaboration.
tasks.still_hard: Trade-offs between access, challenge, staffing and safety require discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Elicit constraints and build an approach colleagues can actually deliver.

reach.task: Coordinate an inclusive program across classes
reach.learn: How shared objectives meet classroom and staffing constraints

evidence.claim: Inclusive activity planning requires contextual collaboration; lesson drafting capabilities alone do not establish collaboration-time savings.

assumptions: Boundary is collaborative program development, excluding separate activity delivery, formal resource approval and original student assessment.

The specialist brings existing needs evidence; colleagues supply expertise and practical constraints during s1 before the approach closes. Clarification and existing capture remain counted. No free accessible-activity, staff-available or agreed-program flag is assumed.
Use existing shared documents and communication first. No new system, extra colleague form or transferred work is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Actual staffing, facilities and shared planning responsibilities
research_questions: Which participation constraints require another professional's judgement before planning can conclude?

already_counted.description: Reciprocal inclusive activity planning and clarification

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Necessary collaboration retains its time; no summary-production baseline is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt instruction to individual age and skill

steps.what: Adapt instructional techniques to students' age, skill and observed response during physical activity

tasks.design: Keep live adaptation of physical instruction with the specialist. Existing materials in {DOCS} can provide examples, while suitability is established through observation and interaction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Effective adaptation changes with student response and the physical context.
tasks.enabler_now: Text rewriting tools exist, but this task establishes no separate text-production share.
tasks.still_hard: A technically plausible activity can remain inaccessible or unsafe for the individual.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion, adjust the demonstration and judge whether the adaptation helps.

reach.task: Adapt a demonstration to an individual learner
reach.learn: How response during instruction changes the next teaching move

evidence.claim: LessonUp supports text rewriting, summarization and translation; the digest does not establish automatic adaptation of live physical instruction.
Live physical teaching adaptation remains an individual professional judgement in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is adapting instruction during activity, excluding separate lesson-material authoring and initial motor assessment. Shared observation episodes are assigned once across related tasks.

Students produce responses during s1 and the specialist observes them before adjusting instruction. Known support information comes from the existing educational team before activity; verification remains within retained time. No free skill-level, successful-adaptation or safe-activity flag is assumed.
Use existing activity guidance and accessible demonstrations first. No new model, delegated observation or maintenance is proposed.
unknowns: Specific communication methods and activity constraints
research_questions: Which adaptations improve participation when tested through direct observation?

already_counted.description: Live observation, instructional judgement and adaptation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Direct adaptation retains its time; text rewriting evidence is not transferred to physical teaching savings.

role.altitude: Protect individualized assessment, supervision and inclusive instruction rather than assuming document tools replace direct specialist work.
reach: Work with special education teachers on accessible demonstrations
Collaborate with instructional coordinators on feasible inclusive activities
skills_to_grow: Distinguish observed needs from inferred labels
Test an adaptation through direct student response
role.ambitious_version: A specialist whose assessment and teaching time stays focused on individual participation.
